messages.content: What is the effect of economic status on happiness levels?

function.name: get_happiness_index
function.description: Fetches the happiness index for a given country or area based on data compiled from global surveys. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

country.description: The country for which to retrieve the happiness index.

year.description: The year for which to retrieve the happiness index.

demographic_group.description: The demographic group for which to retrieve the happiness index. If not specified, the total for all groups will be returned.

message.content:
In general, studies of the World Happiness Report and other surveys show that people in higher‑income brackets tend to report higher levels of life satisfaction than those in lower‑income brackets. However, the relationship is not strictly linear:

| Income group | Typical happiness score (World Happiness Index) |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Low income   | ~4–5 (on a 0–10 scale)                         |
| Middle income| ~5–6                                           |
| High income  | ~6–7                                           |

* The gap between low‑ and high‑income groups is usually the largest, while the difference between middle‑ and high‑income groups is smaller—suggesting diminishing returns after a certain income level.  
* Relative income matters: people compare themselves to peers in their community, so a high absolute income may feel less satisfying if everyone else earns similarly.  
* Other factors (social support, health, freedom, corruption) moderate the effect; in some countries, income explains only a modest portion of overall happiness variation.

Would you like me to pull the latest happiness index for a specific country or year to illustrate this trend?
